newsitem.title: BRAZIL: British trade official impressed by Brazil economy.
newsitem.headline: British trade official impressed by Brazil economy.

text.p: A senior British trade official on Thursday said she was impressed with the changes that have taken place in the Brazilian economy since the government's anti-inflation plan went into effect.

Barbara Roche, under secretary of state for trade and industry in the newly elected Labour government, said she would urge British companies to take greater advantage of trade opportunities with Brazil.

"I have been very impressed by all the changes in the economy that have been made," Roche told reporters in Rio. "The message that I will be taking back is that Brazil is a huge market, it's very developing and there are tremendous opportunities here."

Roche was the first member of the new government to make an official visit to Brazil. The trip comes ahead of Brazilian President Fernando Henrique Cardoso's planned state visit to Britain in December.

Trade between the two countries has become increasingly important. Brazil is currently Britain's largest market in Latin America, with exports worth $1.4 billion in 1996. It also the fastest-growing export market for Britain, with a growth rate of 50 percent this year. Brazilian exports to Britain reached $1.6 billion in 1996.

Roche said Brazil's privatization program presented British companies with a wealth of new opportunities, especially in the energy and telecommunications sectors, where they could offer extensive skill and expertise.
"When I go back to the United Kingdom I will be letting them know that message very strongly," Roche said.
She said both Britain and Brazil were particularly interested in promoting trade involving smaller and medium-sized companies, which often were the leading edge of new technology.

Michael Mowlam, the British Department of Trade and Industry's director of trade promotions, who was travelling with Roche, said the biggest challenge for the government was to convince British business leaders of Brazil's potential.

"There are perceptions about Latin America in Britain which are out of date," Mowlam said. "Even recently in Britain, there's been a perception that Brazil is a very big country, but always the country of the future. We believe now that Brazil is the country of today."

Roche visited Brasilia, Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro during her four-day stay in Brazil and met with Brazilian Foreign Minister Luiz Felipe Lampreia and Commerce and Industry Minister Francisco Dornelles.
